questions.text:
Phosphorus forms a range of different chloride-containing ions and molecules.

Complete the table, showing Lewis structure and name of shape for SbCl4- and AsCl5.
questions.expectedAnswer: SbCl4-: Sb central with 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair -> see-saw (or disphenoidal). AsCl5: As central with 5 bonding pairs -> trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.text:
The Lewis structure and shape for arsenic trichloride, AsCl3, are shown (trigonal pyramidal with one lone pair).

Identify and explain the polarity of AsCl3.
questions.expectedAnswer: AsCl3 is polar. The As-Cl bonds are polar and the trigonal pyramidal shape means the dipoles do not cancel due to asymmetry caused by the lone pair.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies AsCl3 as polar. Merit: Explains using bond polarity and asymmetric arrangement.

questions.text: Justify why the Cl-P-Cl bond angles in AsCl3 are different to those in AsCl5.
questions.expectedAnswer: AsCl3 has four areas of electron density (3 bonding + 1 lone pair) based on tetrahedral arrangement, giving bond angles close to 107 degrees. AsCl5 has five areas of electron density (5 bonding pairs) based on trigonal bipyramidal arrangement, with bond angles of 90 and 120 degrees.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States bond angles. Merit: Identifies different electron geometries. Excellence: Justifies the difference.

questions.text:
Finely powdered phosphorus, P(s), readily reacts with chlorine gas, Cl2(g), in an exothermic reaction to produce phosphorus pentachloride, PCl5(g):

P(s) + 5/2 Cl2(g) -> PCl5(g)

Justify, in terms of the entropy changes of the system and surroundings, why the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.expectedAnswer: System entropy decreases: 2.5 gas molecules and one solid produce one gas molecule (fewer particles, less disorder). However, the reaction is exothermic, so heat released to surroundings greatly increases their entropy. The positive dS_surr outweighs the negative dS_sys, making dS_total positive.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises entropy concept. Merit: Explains system OR surroundings entropy. Excellence: Justifies spontaneity with both.

questions.text:
Complete the table showing electron configuration for:

Br
Ag
Fe3+

Iron, Fe, can form two different ions, Fe2+ and Fe3+. Their ionic radii are compared in the graph below.

Explain why the radius of Fe2+ is larger than Fe3+.
questions.expectedAnswer: Both have the same nuclear charge (29 protons). Fe2+ has more electrons (28) than Fe3+ (27), so there is greater electron-electron repulsion in Fe2+, leading to a larger radius.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies same nuclear charge but different electrons. Merit: Explains repulsion difference.

questions.text:
Identify all types of attractive forces between particles of these substances in their liquid state.

Hydrogen bromide, HBr(l) — DvapH = 17.2 kJ mol-1
Hydrogen fluoride, HF(l) — DvapH = 7.46 kJ mol-1
Bromine, Br2(l) — DvapH = 30.0 kJ mol-1
questions.expectedAnswer: HI: Permanent dipole-dipole, London dispersion forces. HCl: Permanent dipole-dipole, London dispersion forces. Cl2: London dispersion forces only.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly identifies forces for at least two substances.

questions.text: Explain why the DvapH of HI is higher than that of HCl.
questions.expectedAnswer: HI has a larger electron cloud than HCl (iodine has more electrons), resulting in stronger London dispersion forces. This outweighs the slightly stronger dipole-dipole in HCl.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises electron cloud size matters. Merit: Explains difference.

questions.text: Justify why Cl2 has the highest DvapH of the three substances.
questions.expectedAnswer: Despite Cl2 having only London dispersion forces, it has a larger molecular size than HCl, giving stronger London forces. The two chlorine atoms together provide a substantial electron cloud. Its overall intermolecular forces are strongest among these three.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises larger size gives stronger LDF. Merit: Explains Cl2's large size. Excellence: Compares all three.

questions.text:
Nitric acid, H2SO4, is manufactured from nitrogen dioxide. One reaction is:

2NO2(g) + O2(g) -> 2N2O4(g)   DrH = -114 kJ mol-1

Write the balanced equation to represent the standard enthalpy of formation of NO2.

Data: N2O4(g) DfH = +33.2 kJ mol-1, H2O(l) DfH = -286 kJ mol-1
Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation for NO2, DfH(NO2(g)), using the data given.
questions.expectedAnswer: DrH = sum DfH(products) - sum DfH(reactants). -198 = 2(-396) - [2(DfH NO2) + 0]. -198 = -792 - 2x. 2x = -792 + 198 = -594. x = -297 kJ mol-1.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct process with one error. Merit: Correct process. Excellence: Correct answer with units.

questions.text:
Dimethylhydrazine, (CH3)2NNH2, was reacted with dinitrogen tetroxide, N2O4:

2(CH3)2NNH2(l) + N2O4(l) -> 3N2(g) + 4H2O(g)

Calculate DrH using:
(CH3)2NNH2(l) DfH = +50.6 kJ mol-1
CO2(g) DfH = -394 kJ mol-1
N2O4(l) DfH = -19.5 kJ mol-1
H2O(l) DfH = -286 kJ mol-1
H2O(l) -> H2O(g) DvapH = +40.7 kJ mol-1
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly manipulates one value. Merit: Correct process with one error. Excellence: Correct answer.

questions.text: Explain the effect on the standard enthalpy change if the water was produced as a liquid.
questions.expectedAnswer: The enthalpy change would be more exothermic (more negative) because energy is released when water vapour condenses to liquid (intermolecular forces form).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises energy released when gas -> liquid. Merit: Explains fully.

questions.text: Justify, using periodic trends, why strontium, Sr, has a greater first ionisation energy than calcium, Ca.
questions.expectedAnswer: Ca has greater first IE than Ba because Ca has fewer electron shells, meaning outer electrons are closer to the nucleus with less shielding, experiencing a greater effective nuclear charge.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises distance/shielding. Merit: Explains with distance, shielding, and effective nuclear charge.

questions.text:
The atomic radii of five elements from Period 3 are shown.

Na: 0.191 nm, Mg: 0.160 nm, Al: 0.130 nm, Si: 0.118 nm, P: 0.110 nm

Explain the trend in atomic radius.
questions.expectedAnswer: Atomic radius decreases across Period 3 from Na to P. As proton number increases, the nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell. The increased nuclear attraction pulls electrons closer, decreasing radius. Shielding remains roughly constant across the period.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises nuclear charge. Merit: Explains with nuclear charge and same energy level. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
When solid lithium chloride, LiCl(s), dissolves in water, the temperature increases from 20.2 degrees C to 24.8 degrees C.

LiCl(s) -> Mg2+(aq) + SO42-(aq)   DH = -37.0 kJ mol-1

Calculate the mass of LiCl(s) that must dissolve to cause this temperature increase.
Specific heat capacity = 4.18 J g-1 degC-1.
Mass of solution = 85.0 g.
M(LiCl) = 120.4 g mol-1
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculates heat energy. Merit: Correct process with minor error. Excellence: Correct mass with units.
